html:
The most populous country of Central Asia, independent since 1991 and home to the old Silk Road cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva. The map shows it in 1994 and 2010.

Its borders were drawn in 1924, when the Soviet republics were drawn across the lands of the old Uzbek khanates. When the Soviet Union dissolved, the Communist party boss Islam Karimov became president and ruled until his death in 2016. His government allowed no real opposition; in 2005 troops fired on protesters in the Andijan massacre.

Cotton was the economy's backbone, picked with forced labour, including children, at harvest time. Soviet irrigation for cotton drained the rivers that fed the Aral Sea, which shrank to a fraction of its old size. Under Karimov's successor, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the country opened up, and in 2022 its cotton was declared free of forced labour. The capital is Tashkent.
sum: The most populous country of Central Asia, independent since 1991 and home to the old Silk Road cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva. The map shows it in 1994 and 2010.
